what_this_is:
The six errors found by hand in the What Holds Up melanoma draft on 2026-08-26, before publication. They are recorded because they define what factcheck_draft.py exists to catch: any change to its prompts should still surface every class below. Four of the six were inside the draft's own bibliography, which is why the gate never treats a draft's source list as evidence.

Extended 2026-08-27. Until then every entry here named a role in caught_by, so the record logged what the gate found and nothing else. A learning record made only of successes gets better at what it is already good at. The entries below with caught_by 'nothing' are errors that reached a reader, and the entries with caught_by 'a human' are defects in the gate itself. Those two groups are the ones that should drive prompt changes. Use scripts/signal/factcheck_recall.py to check that every class here is still found in the seeded fixture.
found_by: hand check with an adversarial reviewer, pre-publication

errors.caught_by: RECENCY
errors.summary: Draft used three-year KEYNOTE-942 figures; five-year data had been published on 1 June 2026, ten weeks earlier.
errors.why_it_matters: Every figure was correct when first published. Correct-when-written is not a defence.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE
errors.summary: A one-sided p-value was credited to The Lancet. It comes from a company press release; The Lancet published a two-sided value.
errors.was: one-sided p = 0.0266, attributed to the Lancet phase 2b paper
errors.corrected_to: one-sided p = 0.0266 from the Merck release of 16 April 2023; The Lancet published two-sided p = 0.053
errors.why_it_matters: The draft's entire premise is that other people are careless with primary sources.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE
errors.summary: RETRACTED. This entry originally recorded p=0.0075 as a phantom figure appearing in no source. That was wrong: it is stated in Merck's release of 20 January 2026. The real error was DROPPED, recorded below. Kept visible rather than deleted, because a fixture that quietly edits its own history is worth nothing.
errors.was: recorded as: 'a five-year p-value that exists in no locatable source'
errors.corrected_to: reclassified; the figure is real and has been restored to the piece
errors.why_it_matters: The fixture is measured against, so an error in it propagates into every future judgement of whether the gate works.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE
errors.summary: An earlier draft removed a figure as 'unverifiable' that sits in the abstract of a paper the draft itself cited. Two fetch attempts had 403'd and absence of access was read as absence of fact.
errors.was: two-sided p = 0.053 cut, with a footnote saying it could not be verified
errors.corrected_to: restored and cited; it is in the Lancet abstract
errors.why_it_matters: The correction notice was itself false. Failing to reach a source is not evidence about the source.

errors.caught_by: ADVOCATE
errors.summary: One endpoint reported as strengthening over time; a second endpoint that weakened went unmentioned, as did a toxicity difference.
errors.was: 'strengthened rather than faded', with no mention of DMFS easing 62% to 59% or grade 3+ events at 25% vs 18%
errors.corrected_to: both stated explicitly, with the DMFS easing described as inside the noise of a trial that size
errors.why_it_matters: Invisible to a claim-by-claim check. Every individual figure was true.

errors.caught_by: ADVOCATE
errors.summary: The draft accused news outlets of passing off an earlier trial's figures as the new trial's, without checking a single outlet. All of them had attributed correctly.
errors.was: 'being used to fill the hole where the Phase 3's numbers should be, mostly without saying so'
errors.corrected_to: accusation cut; replaced with what a survey of nineteen articles actually found, including the admission that the first draft was wrong
errors.why_it_matters: A claim about third-party conduct, asserted rather than checked. The most likely of the six to be quoted back at the publication.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE
errors.summary: SECOND INSTANCE, found by the gate on its first run. The hand check's own correction notice claimed two figures were unverifiable. Both are verifiable. Failure to reach a source was recorded as the figure not existing — the same error the notice was describing.
errors.was: 'a five-year p-value of 0.0075 that appears in no source we can find, now removed' and '2.5-year recurrence-free rates of 74.8% versus 55.6%' cut as unverifiable
errors.corrected_to: both restored: one-sided nominal p=0.0075 is in Merck's release of 20 January 2026; 74.8% vs 55.6% is the 30-month rate in the three-year analysis
errors.why_it_matters: The error class repeats under pressure. A checker that says CANNOT VERIFY is reporting on its own reach, not on the world, and must never be paraphrased as the fact being absent.

errors.caught_by: ADVOCATE
errors.summary: The Phase 3 was described as 'free of the bias the earlier one carried'. Its primary endpoint is investigator-assessed too, per Merck's own release.
errors.was: 'seven times larger and free of the bias the earlier one carried'
errors.corrected_to: 'blinded against exactly the bias the earlier one carried', plus a new paragraph noting the primary endpoint is 'as assessed by the investigator' and that blinding mitigates rather than removes it
errors.why_it_matters: Invisible to a claim check: every figure was right. Only a reader arguing the subject's side finds it.

errors.summary: A hazard ratio converted into a count of people. 'It is consistent with the therapy preventing five deaths in six' — HR 0.165 is an estimated 84% lower HAZARD of death, not five deaths in six prevented.
errors.found_by: outside editorial review of issue one, 2026-08-27
errors.caught_by: INFERENCE
errors.why_it_survived: SOURCE verified the interval 0.165-1.345 against the primary source and passed it, because the figure was real. The error was in the sentence built on it. No role was reading for that.
errors.aggravating: The same piece explains the hazard-ratio versus absolute-risk distinction correctly two paragraphs earlier. A reader who understood our own explanation would have caught us.
errors.was: It is consistent with the therapy preventing five deaths in six, and with it doing harm.
errors.corrected_to: The interval is extraordinarily wide: compatible with anything from a very large reduction in the hazard of death to roughly a 35% increase.

errors.summary: A criticism valid for the open-label phase 2 trial applied to the double-blind phase 3 trial. 'Blinding does not eliminate the problem', and the claim that an independent review committee would 'remove the judgement altogether' — an IRC relocates judgment to blinded central assessors, it does not remove it.
errors.found_by: outside editorial review of issue one, 2026-08-27
errors.caught_by: INFERENCE
errors.why_it_survived: Every factual component was true and ADVOCATE read it as fair comment. The defect was that the criticism named no residual mechanism surviving the design.
errors.was: blinding does not eliminate the problem; an independent review committee would remove the judgement altogether
errors.corrected_to: RFS is investigator-assessed rather than centrally adjudicated. That leaves clinical judgment in the endpoint determination, although the double-blind placebo-controlled design substantially protects against differential assessment between arms.

errors.summary: 'The Phase 3 announcement reports no Phase 3 results.' It reports a result — that the trial met its prespecified RFS and DMFS endpoints. What it does not report is any numerical efficacy estimate.
errors.found_by: outside editorial review of issue one, 2026-08-27
errors.caught_by: INFERENCE
errors.why_it_survived: Rhetorically effective and nearly true, which is the hardest kind to catch. One word — 'numerical' — makes the thesis almost impossible to dispute at no cost to its force.
errors.was: The Phase 3 announcement reports no Phase 3 results.
errors.corrected_to: The Phase 3 announcement reports no numerical Phase 3 efficacy results.

errors.summary: 'The endpoint people actually care about — whether anyone lives longer.' Recurrence-free and metastasis-free survival are clinically meaningful outcomes in adjuvant melanoma, and FDA has approved therapies in this setting on RFS.
errors.found_by: outside editorial review of issue one, 2026-08-27
errors.caught_by: INFERENCE
errors.why_it_survived: It reads as a methodological observation and is actually a value judgment. Nothing in a claim-by-claim check tests for that.
errors.was: the endpoint people actually care about - whether anyone lives longer
errors.corrected_to: RFS and OS answer different questions. The trial answered the first; the second remains open. FDA has approved adjuvant melanoma therapies on RFS.

errors.summary: SOURCE returned NOT_FOUND for a page that exists and contains the exact claim, verbatim, while COVERAGE had already cited the same page with its URL in the same run.
errors.was: no article or post from that site containing this specific claim could be located through multiple targeted searches, so the claim cannot be verified
errors.corrected_to: The article is at morningglorysciences.com, dated 20 August 2026, and reads: 'The Phase 2b population was stage IIIB-IV; the Phase 3 adds stage IIB and IIC - node-negative disease. Absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit.'
errors.caught_by: a human asking why nobody had opened the page
errors.why_it_survived: SOURCE searches; it was never handed the URL. COVERAGE had the URL and did not pass it on. Two roles in one run reached opposite conclusions about the same page and neither could see the other's work. NOT_FOUND from SOURCE means 'we could not reach it', and the gate treats it as a blocker, which is right — but the resolution is to open the page, and nothing in the output said so.

errors.caught_by: nothing — it reached subscribers
errors.summary: 'Met both of its endpoints' for a trial with one primary endpoint (RFS) and one key secondary (DMFS). Implies two co-primaries and overstates what the announcement established.
errors.was: a large Phase 3 trial of a personalised mRNA cancer therapy met both of its endpoints in melanoma
errors.corrected_to: met its primary endpoint in melanoma, and a key secondary endpoint as well
errors.found_by: SOURCE, on a run after the broadcast had been sent
errors.why_it_survived: The page had it right from the start — 'its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and its key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival' — and the email, written from the page, compressed it. Nothing checked the email against the page. The claim extractor produced 'the trial met both pre-specified endpoints', which reads as true unless you already know the endpoint structure, so SOURCE had to go to the release to catch it and only did on a later run.
errors.why_it_matters: The error is invisible to anyone who does not already know the trial design, which is most readers, and it inflates the result in exactly the direction the piece accuses others of inflating it.

errors.caught_by: nothing — it reached subscribers
errors.summary: '157 unblinded patients' for a trial that was open-label from the start. Unblinded implies a blind that was broken, which is a worse and different design failure.
errors.was: 157 unblinded patients is not 1,137 blinded ones
errors.corrected_to: 157 patients in an open-label trial is not 1,137 in a double-blind one
errors.found_by: INFERENCE, MINOR, on a later run
errors.why_it_survived: Every figure in the sentence was correct, so SOURCE passed it. It is not unfair to the subject in a way ADVOCATE would flag. It is a word that means something adjacent to what was meant, and only the statistical role reads at that resolution — and rated it MINOR, which does not block.
errors.why_it_matters: A publication whose subject is imprecision in others cannot afford a term of art used loosely, and MINOR is the severity at which this class will always land.

errors.caught_by: nothing — the broadcast went out
errors.summary: Every correction made to the page that afternoon was absent from the email that went to subscribers, including an accusation against seven named outlets that had already been cut from the page.
errors.was: an email whose text no gate run had ever seen
errors.corrected_to: send_broadcast.py now refuses unless a gate report exists, records passed true, and its sha256 matches the content Resend actually stores
errors.why_it_survived: The gate checked drafts. Nothing checked what was sent. Two artefacts, one checked, and the unchecked one was the one that reached people.
errors.why_it_matters: The most expensive failure in the project so far was not a wrong number. It was a correct number that never reached the thing being published.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE, next run
errors.summary: Correcting a vague date by naming a specific one created two new wrong claims. 'Released in January and presented at ASCO in June' — January carried the RFS figure only; the DMFS figure and the OS hazard ratio the piece then dissects were both first public at ASCO in June.
errors.was: whose five-year results were released in January and presented at ASCO in June
errors.corrected_to: whose five-year results were presented at ASCO in June
errors.found_by: SOURCE returned two WRONG_VALUEs and ADVOCATE a SERIOUS on the same clause
errors.why_it_survived: The fetch that established the January date said in the same response that the January release did not contain the 59% figure. The refutation was on screen and the sentence was written anyway. Across three passes of issue one the unverified-claim count went 7, 6, 13, and the rise was almost entirely claims added while fixing earlier findings.
errors.why_it_matters: This is the mechanism behind most of the churn. Every fix is a new claim, and a new claim is unverified until it is verified. The publication criterion exists for this: no claim added in a pass that is not itself verified.

errors.caught_by: a human reading past the header line
errors.summary: SOURCE returned WRONG_VALUE twice in one run while the note beneath each said the draft was right. One read: 'the trial did enroll stage IIIB-IV, so VERIFIED is more accurate than WRONG_VALUE. Revising to VERIFIED.'
errors.was: [WRONG_VALUE] stage IIIB-IV ... note: the claim is not materially wrong
errors.corrected_to: recorded as decisions; the draft was not changed
errors.why_it_survived: The role reasons in the note and then fills the verdict field, and nothing checks that the two agree. The report prints the verdict in the header and the note four lines down, so a run reads as two failures at a glance and as zero on reading. SECOND OCCURRENCE 2026-08-28, on the CDK4/6 draft: SOURCE checked MONARCH 3's HR 0.80 (0.64-1.02) against the publication's 0.804 (0.637-1.015), reasoned through the rounding in its own note, wrote 'On closer inspection both rounded values are consistent with the source values, so this is within normal rounding. Revising to VERIFIED' -- and emitted WRONG_VALUE. The note is the model's working and the verdict is a separate field it does not revisit.
errors.why_it_matters: It inflates the apparent error rate of drafts that are correct, which is the direction that causes needless editing — and needless editing is what introduces FIX_INTRODUCED_THE_ERROR.

errors.caught_by: a human checking the registry and the literature
errors.summary: ADVOCATE asserted across three runs that KEYNOTE-942 used blinded independent central review for RFS and DMFS, escalating to SERIOUS on the strength of it, and never cited a source. Three sources say otherwise.
errors.was: KEYNOTE-942 ... endpoints (RFS, DMFS) were assessed by blinded independent central review — the standard safeguard against open-label bias
errors.corrected_to: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03897881 gives masking NONE and describes the primary outcome only as assessed using radiological imaging; the Lancet abstract describes an open-label trial and names no central review; NCCN's JNCCN 360 report of the ASCO 2024 update says endpoints included investigator-assessed relapse-free survival
errors.why_it_survived: Roles that cite URLs are checkable and roles that do not are not. SOURCE returns a url field; ADVOCATE and INFERENCE return prose. An assertion of fact inside a fairness objection gets the authority of a finding without the evidence of one.
errors.why_it_matters: A SERIOUS objection blocks publication. One that rests on an unsourced factual claim can block a correct draft indefinitely, and the third appearance came back hedged to 'in some analyses', which is a source-shaped phrase with no source behind it.

errors.caught_by: a human reading the NOT_FOUND list
errors.summary: The extractor sent the publication's own disclosure lines out to be web-searched. SOURCE went looking for CivicScale, found Civica and CivicHealth, and reported it could not verify that the company exists.
errors.was: [NOT_FOUND] CivicScale sells healthcare software and takes no outside investment
errors.corrected_to: marked internal; no external source can confirm a claim about our own funding
errors.why_it_survived: The extractor marks some claims internal and missed these across two runs. Once mis-scoped, SOURCE behaves correctly — it genuinely cannot verify them — so the failure looks like a finding rather than a routing error.
errors.why_it_matters: Same direction as VERDICT_CONTRADICTS_ITS_OWN_NOTE: it makes a clean draft read as a failing one.

errors.caught_by: the recall test, 2026-08-27
errors.summary: ADVOCATE found no instance of the UNSUPPORTED class on a draft that contains one, and it was the only class no role found at all.
errors.was: They are being used to fill the hole where the Phase 3's numbers should be, mostly without saying so.
errors.corrected_to: a mandatory sweep of every party the draft characterises other than the subject, added to the prompt
errors.why_it_survived: The prompt already lists 'unsupported characterisation of anyone's conduct — ours, a regulator's, another publication's'. The persona is the subject's head of communications, and an accusation against news outlets costs the subject nothing, so the motivation never fires on the bullet that is already there. Nobody in the gate represents the third parties a draft criticises.
errors.why_it_matters: This is the class of the accusation against seven named outlets that went out in the broadcast and that an outside reviewer flagged. It is the fairness failure most likely to cost credibility, and until now the gate could not see it.

errors.caught_by: the recall test, 2026-08-27
errors.summary: INFERENCE found the first instance of MISSING_NUMBER_AS_MISSING_EVIDENCE and missed a second instance of the same class four paragraphs later.
errors.was: Of the 1,137-patient trial it is announcing, the quantitative content is nil.
errors.corrected_to: REPORT EVERY INSTANCE, NOT EVERY CLASS added to both prompts
errors.why_it_survived: The roles return a list of findings and treat a class as discharged once reported. Nothing asks for exhaustiveness within a class.
errors.why_it_matters: The endpoint error that reached subscribers is exactly this shape: the page had it right and the email had it wrong, and one instance found is one instance fixed.

errors.caught_by: the recall test, 2026-08-27
errors.summary: RECENCY assessed nine studies on a draft seeded with three stale-figure errors and reported none superseded. All three were caught instead by SOURCE, and only as NOT_FOUND.
errors.was: 0 superseded or unknown, on a draft quoting three-year intervals for a trial whose five-year data it cites by name
errors.corrected_to: the prompt now requires pulling the specific figures out of the draft and comparing each against the latest publication
errors.why_it_survived: It was answering whether a newer readout exists. It does, and the draft cites it, so every study read as CURRENT. The stale figures sat inside a draft that named the current source.
errors.why_it_matters: STALE looked covered because SOURCE happened to catch all three — but as NOT_FOUND, the verdict whose own guidance says it means 'we could not reach a source, not that none exists'. A stale figure that still matches its original source cleanly would pass SOURCE and pass RECENCY, and that is the definition of the class: correct when written.

errors.caught_by: reading the first recall run's output line by line
errors.summary: factcheck_recall.py scored each seeded error against every finding independently, so one INFERENCE finding satisfied two seeded errors four paragraphs apart. The first run reported recall of 12 of 14 when it was 11.
errors.was: HAZARD_AS_RISK reported FOUND, matched to the finding about RATIO_AS_LIVES at 0.9
errors.corrected_to: greedy one-to-one assignment: highest-scoring pair first, then the finding is spent
errors.why_it_survived: The matcher was tested against hand-written paraphrases, one per seed, which is precisely the case that cannot expose it.
errors.why_it_matters: A measurement that flatters the instrument is worse than no measurement, because it gets believed. This one was built to answer whether the gate can be trusted and its first answer was half a point too generous.

errors.caught_by: run v2 printing '[FOUND] ... nothing came close' on the same line
errors.summary: factcheck_recall.py read RECENCY findings from keys the role does not return — cited_as, study, newer — where the schema is name, draft_uses, latest_known, status, what_changed. Every RECENCY finding carried an empty quote.
errors.was: STALE [FOUND] expect RECENCY / nothing came close
errors.corrected_to: draft_uses or name, and the status filter reads CURRENT rather than a 'newer' key that does not exist
errors.why_it_survived: The matcher's text channel joined every string value, so RECENCY still matched on figures and the recall number was right. Only the display was wrong, which is the kind of defect that survives because nothing fails.
errors.why_it_matters: It made the first run's verdict on RECENCY unreadable, and the first run's verdict on RECENCY was the main finding — a role that had found nothing looked the same as a role whose output could not be read.

errors.caught_by: SELECTIVE reading as a blind spot in run v2 after being found in run v1
errors.summary: Two seeded errors live in one sentence — stale safety figures and a selective read of them. One-to-one assignment gave the finding to whichever seed scored higher and reported the other as MISSED against an unrelated best match.
errors.was: BLIND SPOTS — SELECTIVE, on a run where ADVOCATE returned seven objections
errors.corrected_to: the loser is now reported with the finding that outscored it, and a note that a human has to read whether that finding is about both faults or only one
errors.why_it_survived: One-to-one assignment was added to stop one finding being credited to two seeds, which was a real bug. The fix is right in general and wrong for the case where two genuinely different faults occupy the same sentence, and the fixture contains exactly one such case.
errors.why_it_matters: A blind spot is the most consequential thing this test reports. One that is an artefact of the scoring rule would send us to rewrite a prompt that is working.

errors.caught_by: a human opening the company release, three times
errors.summary: SOURCE reports a figure as wrong by comparing it against an earlier readout of the same trial. The numbers it returns are real; they are from the wrong analysis.
errors.was: adverse events 59.6/59.6/51.0 called wrong against the 2023 primary analysis, then against the three-year update; five-year RFS rates called a timepoint conflation when both bounds were five-year
errors.corrected_to: the prompt now requires establishing that the source describes the same data cut before returning WRONG_VALUE, and NOT_FOUND when it cannot
errors.why_it_survived: The role's evidence looks impeccable — a real figure from a real primary source — so the finding reads as solid unless a human already knows which readout is which. RECENCY had the right answer in the same run all three times and the two roles cannot see each other.
errors.why_it_matters: It manufactures errors in correct drafts, which is the direction that causes needless editing, and needless editing is what introduces real errors.

errors.caught_by: ADVOCATE and INFERENCE and COVERAGE, all three, on the CDK4/6 draft
errors.summary: The draft takes a term of art from a source document, reads it more broadly than the field does, and then accuses the source of overstating on the strength of our reading. Every fact in the sentence is true and the accusation still does not hold.
errors.was: 'The record that the drugs have not been directly compared in clinical trials is broader than the evidence supports - the real-world cohort is a direct comparison of all three. It is not randomised. It is direct.' In guideline language 'directly compared in clinical trials' means a randomised head-to-head trial. The real-world study we cited as the counter-example opens by describing its own purpose as working in the absence of randomised trials that directly compare the three.
errors.corrected_to: the charge withdrawn and replaced with the opposite finding - that the guideline is accurate as written, and that what the two comparisons add is the only evidence on a question it correctly records as untested
errors.why_it_survived: It is not a wrong figure, so SOURCE passes it. It is not unfair to the subject in the ordinary sense, because the subject's own sentence is quoted accurately. It reads as the piece's sharpest observation, which is exactly what makes it dangerous: the sentence a draft is proudest of is the one nobody re-reads.
errors.why_it_matters: Second occurrence in two issues. Issue one accused the coverage of passing off an earlier trial's figures without checking an outlet; issue two accused a guideline of overstating a limitation on a definition we supplied ourselves. The shape is identical - a publication about other people's imprecision reaching for a scalp - and it is the class most likely to be quoted back at us, because the injured party is a named institution that can answer.

errors.caught_by: nothing - the page went to the gate without it
errors.found_by: reading the working brief after the gate reported the omission, 2026-08-28
errors.summary: A fact the working brief recorded in its own table did not reach the page, and nothing compared the two. The gate then spent four serious findings rediscovering it.
errors.was: issues/WHU-002-cdk46/draft.md carried a fifth column, 'OS significant' - MONARCH 3 no, MONALEESA-2 yes, MONALEESA-7 yes, PALOMA-2 no. The HTML table has four columns. The significance status of every overall-survival result was dropped in transcription, in a piece whose entire argument is about what the significance threshold decides.
errors.corrected_to: the column restored to the page and the p-values stated in the argument as well as the table
errors.why_it_survived: No role can find it. Every figure that reached the page is correct and the gate cannot see a document it was not given. This is not a research failure or a writing failure - the research was done and written down. It is a handoff with no check across it.
errors.why_it_matters: The expensive kind of omission is the one where we already had the answer. A mechanical diff of the brief's figures against the page's, before the gate runs, costs nothing and would have caught this. The gate cost $3.96 and caught it four times over.

errors.caught_by: SOURCE, WRONG_VALUE, twice in one run
errors.summary: Figures were copied out of a secondary document -- a guideline -- into a table of our own, carrying that document's rounding conventions and its choice of readout, without going back to the trial publications. The secondary document was accurate. The table was not.
errors.was: PALOMA-2 overall survival printed as 0.78-1.20. The guideline prints 0.78-1.2; the publication gives 0.777-1.177, which is 1.18. We added a decimal place the source did not claim, in the one sentence of the piece that is about where an upper bound falls. Separately, MONALEESA-2's PFS was carried as 0.56 (0.45-0.70), the guideline's truncation of 0.568 (0.457-0.704), and MONARCH 3's PFS as the 2017 registrational readout in a row whose OS column held the 2024 final analysis.
errors.corrected_to: every figure re-derived from the trial publication, each trial's PFS and OS taken from the same analysis, bounds rounded rather than truncated, and MONALEESA-7's OS labelled as the exploratory analysis it is
errors.why_it_survived: The source was authoritative and its figures were correct, so nothing about the row looked wrong. A guideline rounds for a reader deciding treatment, where a hundredth changes nothing, and cites the registrational readout because that is what a guideline cites. Both conventions are right for that document and wrong for a piece whose argument is the position of interval bounds.
errors.why_it_matters: Three charges against the guideline were tested in this issue and all three failed: it did not overstate the absence of direct comparison, it did not misprint the intervals, and it did not mix readouts -- we did, by importing its row into a table it was never built for. The rule this yields is flat: a secondary document tells you which trial to read, never what the trial found.

errors.caught_by: a human reading the second run against the first
errors.summary: A class added to this file on the morning of the same day was quoted back by the role it was written for, by name, to justify a false positive. The first measured instance of the over-firing this file's own header warns about.
errors.was: SOURCE_PRECISION_IMPORTED_UNCHECKED was recorded after the draft printed 1.20 where the guideline printed 1.2. On the next run, SOURCE flagged the corrected figure -- HR 0.96 (0.78-1.18), rounded from the JCO paper's 0.956 (0.777-1.177) -- as WRONG_VALUE, with the note 'a SOURCE_PRECISION_IMPORTED_UNCHECKED pattern'. Ordinary two-decimal rounding of a hazard ratio, called an error because a class name existed for something adjacent.
errors.corrected_to: declined in draft_decisions.json with the reasoning written out. The recall brief is not changed yet: one instance is not a rate.
errors.why_it_survived: Nothing catches it. A role given a list of past mistakes will find them, and a finding that names a real recorded class reads as better evidenced than one that does not. The name is doing the work the evidence should.
errors.why_it_matters: The header of this file predicted exactly this and told us to measure it with factcheck_recall.py before and after any change to the recall block. Three classes were added on 2026-08-28 and recall was not run. Run it. A learning record that makes the instrument worse is worse than no learning record, and the direction of the damage -- manufactured errors in correct drafts -- is the one the WRONG_READOUT_COMPARISON entry already names as the costly one.

errors.caught_by: running it as instructed and reading the two reports side by side
errors.summary: This file tells you to run factcheck_recall.py before and after any change to the recall block. Run once per arm, that instruction cannot answer the question: the gate is a sampler, and two runs of the identical fixture differ on half the rows for reasons that have nothing to do with the change.
errors.was: Same fixture, same code, only the recall brief differing by four classes. 8 of 15 seeded errors changed verdict between the two runs. Net: found 11 -> 12, missed 4 -> 3, mislabelled 0 -> 3. Three separate rows swapped between FOUND and FOUND BY ANOTHER ROLE, which is pure role-attribution noise. OVERSTATED went FOUND -> MISSED although it is in both briefs and nothing about it changed.
errors.corrected_to: nothing yet. The one change with a mechanism behind it -- SOURCE_FAULTED_ON_OUR_OWN_DEFINITION was a blind spot before the class existed and was found after -- is recorded as directional evidence and not as a result. Every other difference is treated as noise until measured at n >= 3 per arm.
errors.why_it_survived: The instruction reads as complete. 'Run it before and after' is what you would write if you had not yet watched the thing move on its own, and the file was written before anyone had. Nobody had run it twice on the same input.
errors.why_it_matters: The whole point of the recall test is to stop the learning record from making the instrument worse. An underpowered test does not merely fail to detect harm -- it licenses the change, because someone runs it, sees 11 -> 12, and ships. Three runs per arm at roughly $2 a run is $12 to answer a question we are currently answering with a coin. Until that is budgeted, the honest position is that the effect of the 2026-08-28 classes on the instrument is unknown.

errors.caught_by: reading the error line, which printed the response it had rejected
errors.summary: The JSON salvage scanned for the first '{' or '[' in a response and committed to it. Roles in this file write about intervals and citations, so their prose is full of brackets. One bracket before the answer and three API calls were spent rejecting an answer the model had already given correctly.
errors.was: source:MONALEESA-2 failed three times; the printed tail was a well-formed array ending in a closing code fence. Two roles hit the same fault in one run and RECENCY hit it twice in the run before, at about $0.74. The retries are charged in full.
errors.corrected_to: strip code fences, try every candidate start rather than the first, and rank what parses by whether it has the shape of an answer -- an object, a list of objects, or an empty list. Covered by backend/tests/signal/test_json_salvage.py, 13 cases.
errors.why_it_survived: It looks like a model failure and reads like one in the log: 'response was not JSON'. The error line was already printing the evidence that it was JSON, and nobody had read it. Retries hid the cost as spend rather than as breakage.
errors.why_it_matters: The second-order failure is worse than the waste. A preamble such as 'Per the paper [1], the result:' contains a VALID array, and the old salvage would return [1] -- silently accepted as 'this role found nothing'. That is a clean pass on a check that never ran, which is the one output of this gate that must never be manufacturable by accident.

errors.caught_by: the truncation detector added earlier the same day
errors.summary: A fixed output budget ran out, was raised for the one role that hit it, and ran out again a few hours later on the role beside it. Every role in the file reads the whole draft; there was never a reason for one of them to have a different cap.
errors.was: max_tokens was a constant 8,000, set when the only draft was 8,000 characters. Extraction overflowed at 27,647 characters and was given a draft-scaled budget. INFERENCE overflowed at 33,000 with the same constant, four runs later. The second failure was invisible before that morning's other fix: a truncated response used to print 'response was not JSON', retry twice at full price, and return nothing -- reported as a role with zero findings, which reads exactly like a clean check.
errors.corrected_to: one read_budget() shared by extraction, RECENCY, ADVOCATE, INFERENCE and COVERAGE, scaled to the draft
errors.why_it_survived: The first fix was made under the pressure of a failing run, at the site of the failure, and it worked. Nothing then asked whether anything else had the same constant. The class was visible in one grep.
errors.why_it_matters: The failure mode is silent. A role that returns nothing looks identical in the report to a role that found nothing, and this gate's entire value is that an unrun check is not a pass. It was caught here only because a separate fix that morning taught the caller to distinguish 'cut off' from 'malformed'. Without that, run 14 would have reported a clean statistical check on a draft it never finished reading.

errors.caught_by: the outside reviewer, who opened the paper
errors.found_by: outside review of the CDK4/6 assessment, 2026-08-29
errors.summary: A finding the gate generated about somebody else's published work was written onto the page without anyone opening that work. It was wrong. No number of further gate runs could have caught it, because the gate produced it and no role audits another role's output.
errors.was: RECENCY reported, on three separate runs, that the Scientific Reports network meta-analysis had used MONARCH 3's interim overall-survival figure (HR 0.754) rather than the final (0.804). The page said so, and framed it as a disclosure -- 'the input is out of date, and we would rather say so than have it found'. The paper's Table 1 lists MONARCH 3 at HR 0.804 (0.637-1.015), 97.2 months, 'year of updated data 2023', citing the SABCS 2023 final analysis. It had used the final figure all along.
errors.corrected_to: the claim withdrawn and replaced with the sourced opposite, with the correction recorded on the page. The RECENCY section of every report now carries a banner saying that its findings are claims about documents the role has not opened, and each stale study carries the line 'BEFORE ACTING: open the source above and read the sentence.'
errors.why_it_survived: Self-criticism reads as verified. A sentence that admits a weakness in our own evidence gets less scrutiny than one that asserts a strength, and this one borrowed the credibility of a disclosure for an unchecked assertion about a third party. Three gate runs repeated it and each repetition made it look more settled.
errors.why_it_matters: This is the class the publication exists to find in other people, committed against a named research group, on the strength of our own instrument. It is also the clearest available argument for the outside review step: fourteen gate runs could not see it, and one reader with the table open saw it immediately.

errors.caught_by: the eighth firing of the same finding, and reading it properly
errors.summary: A finding was dismissed as an over-fire seven consecutive times, recorded in this fixture as RECALL_BRIEF_OVERFIRED_A_NEW_CLASS, and was right. Each dismissal made the next one faster, and the recorded dismissal became the reason for the dismissals that followed it -- the fixture entry meant to stop a bad check from wasting attention instead stopped a good check from getting any.
errors.was: 1.015 printed as 1.02, dismissed as correct rounding
errors.should_have_been: 1.015 at the one sentence whose argument is where that bound landed. The rounding was correct; the precision claim was not. And the rounding was asymmetric -- 0.804 down to 0.80, 1.015 up to 1.02 -- which widened the apparent gap in the direction that flattered the argument.
errors.why_it_survived: Nothing in the process distinguishes 'we considered this and it is fine' from 'we stopped reading it'. Both look identical in draft_decisions.json, and the second is what a seventh identical dismissal actually is. The role's argument had been getting sharper each run and nobody was reading it closely enough to notice.

errors.caught_by: a second post-publication review, which searched for the counterexample
errors.found_by: post-publication review of the CDK4/6 assessment, 2026-08-29
errors.summary: A claim was verified as something a source SAYS and then written as something WE KNOW. NCCN v6.2026 states 'the CDK4/6 inhibitors have not been directly compared in clinical trials'. The source advocate asked whether the guideline says this; the operator opened the guideline and confirmed the exact sentence. That verification was of a quotation. The page then wrote 'No randomised trial has tested one of these drugs against another' as its own unscoped assertion about the world, and went further -- 'In guideline language, directly compared in clinical trials means a randomised head-to-head trial, and none exists.'
errors.was: No randomised trial has compared any of the three against another
errors.should_have_been: Either the attributed form -- 'the guideline records that they have not been directly compared' -- or a claim we had actually checked against the world. A randomised phase III open-label trial of ribociclib vs palbociclib, each with fulvestrant, was published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention in 2024 (PFS 12.69 vs 13.67 months, no significant difference), and HARMONIA (NCT05207709, SOLTI-2101/AFT-58) is a registered head-to-head phase III of the same two drugs.
errors.why_it_survived: Confirming that a source says X is not confirming X, and nothing in the pipeline distinguishes the two. Worse, the guideline's sentence is scoped to the first-line AI setting it is discussing, and the scope was dropped in the adoption. The missed trial's result AGREES with the page's conclusion, so the omission did not bias the argument -- it made our claim broader than we could support while making our evidence base look thinner than it was.

errors.caught_by: asking where each agreeing source got it
errors.found_by: post-publication review of the CDK4/6 assessment, 2026-08-29
errors.summary: The COVERAGE role reported multiple sources agreeing that no head-to-head comparison exists. Every one of them was downstream of the same claim: NCCN summaries repeating the guideline, and P-VERIFY, which the page itself quotes as describing its purpose as working 'in the absence of randomised trials that directly compare the three'. The page cited that as confirmation. It is an echo.
errors.was: several independent sources agree, so the claim is well supported
errors.should_have_been: Sources that descend from one upstream document are one source. Count independent derivations, not agreeing documents.
errors.why_it_survived: The gate counts agreement and has no notion of independence, so a claim everybody repeats reads as a claim everybody has checked.

errors.caught_by: the reviewer running the obvious query we never ran
errors.found_by: post-publication review of the CDK4/6 assessment, 2026-08-29
errors.summary: The comparative-evidence section was framed as 'indirect comparisons', and the searches went looking for network meta-analyses and real-world cohorts. A search framed as 'what indirect comparisons exist' cannot return a randomised trial. The plain question -- has anyone randomised these against each other? -- was never asked, and neither registry was ever searched.
errors.was: four indirect comparisons are the comparative evidence
errors.should_have_been: A registry query for the two drug names plus 'randomized' returns HARMONIA on the first page. Trials that terminate early or publish outside the high-visibility journals do not surface in a literature-and-coverage sweep and are in the registry.
errors.why_it_survived: Every search was framed by the conclusion we had already reached. This is the premise-fitting failure that the entry gate addresses at the level of the piece, recurring at the level of a single load-bearing sentence.

errors.caught_by: committing the same error twice in one document, and once more the next day
errors.found_by: post-publication review of the CDK4/6 assessment, 2026-08-29
errors.summary: Three standing rules in this repository failed to fire at the moment of writing. (1) After MONALEESA-7 we recorded that treating a fact as unknowable because we could not open one paper 'was turning a number we had not found into evidence that did not exist' -- and then wrote exactly that about MONALEESA-2's test direction, four sections later, when it is on ClinicalTrials.gov's results tab. (2) GATE_CLAIM_ABOUT_A_THIRD_PARTY_PUBLISHED_UNCHECKED, whose banner prints on every RECENCY output, did not stop 'Jacot and colleagues' being taken from gate output and printed as an attribution; the paper is by Tanguy et al. and contains no Jacot. That was introduced while FIXING an attribution gap. (3) The universal-quantifier lint produced the list containing 'No randomised trial has compared any of the three' and nobody was required to act on it.
errors.was: the rule is in the fixture and in the role prompts
errors.should_have_been: A check in code at the moment of writing. The two rules that became code -- the source ledger and the deterministic lint -- are the two that fired. Prose in a fixture is a reminder for someone already looking.
errors.why_it_survived: A checklist nobody is required to act on is documentation, not a control.

errors.caught_by: the entry gate's kill condition, before drafting — and the day before, by a reviewer, after publication
errors.summary: Twice in two days the thing we were about to present as our own contribution was already in print. On 28-29 August the page argued that MONARCH 3's wider interval reflected trial power rather than drug effect; Tanguy et al. made that argument formally in npj Breast Cancer in 2018 and we found it only through a gate run, after writing it. On 29 August a candidate proposed separating the tobacco analogy into its evidentiary legs; Tibor Rutar had published exactly that, in four sections with citations, on 2 April 2026.
errors.was: we identified a gap in the coverage
errors.should_have_been: 'The coverage missed this' is a universal negative over everything anyone has published, and it is the single claim this publication makes in every issue. It gets the same adversarial treatment as any other universal negative: one call whose job is to find the person who already said it.
errors.why_it_survived: We search for evidence that supports the premise with far more energy than we search for someone who got there first, because the first search feels like research and the second feels like looking for a reason to stop. The counterexample hunter was built for universal negatives ON the page and was never pointed at the premise behind it.

errors.caught_by: four consecutive candidates dying on prior art in eight hours
errors.summary:
Four subjects were killed in one session because the finding was already published: the MONARCH 3 power argument (Tanguy et al. 2018, found after we wrote it); the tobacco evidentiary comparison (Rutar, April 2026); 'what evidence would settle this' (National Academies 2024, plus Piccardi et al. in Science 2025 falsifying the premise outright); and the audit of Australia's cited evidence (Horwood et al. 2026, citing four earlier critiques).

In every case the prior art was in the ACADEMIC record and we had been reading the NEWS record. The premise 'wide coverage missed a fact readers would want' is usually false in its first half and true in its second: the fact is rarely missed, it is published in a journal the reader will never open.
errors.was: find what everyone missed
errors.should_have_been: Find what the specialists established and the coverage never carried. That is a translation function rather than a discovery function: it credits rather than claims, it is achievable by a small operation, and it survives the prior-art check by construction, because the prior art IS the material.
errors.why_it_survived: The entry gate asks whether anyone has said this. On any contested scientific or policy question the answer is almost always yes, so the gate kills every candidate and the publication has nothing to write. The question it should ask is whether anyone has said it where a general reader would find it.

errors.caught_by: clearing the open items before drafting
errors.summary: A candidate was built on the claim that a Forbes piece of August 2026 was still carrying a misread of a June 2025 preprint, thirteen months after Ethan Mollick corrected it. The Forbes piece does not cite the preprint. It argues from general neuroplasticity. The chain was inferred from a headline that sounded like the study's conclusion.
errors.was: the belief travels in Forbes, the correction travels in Substack
errors.should_have_been: Two documents on the same topic are not thereby linked. Every claim of the form 'A is carrying B' is a claim about a citation, and a citation is a thing you open the document and look for.
errors.why_it_survived: Nothing checks the relationship BETWEEN sources. The ledger records whether we opened each document; the inherited-claims file records what we took from each. Neither asks whether a link we assert between two of them exists. This is the same shape as the endnote-17 finding — where we caught a government treating two citations as independent when one contained the other — arrived at from the opposite direction.

errors.caught_by: opening the four counterexamples the hunter returned
errors.summary: The counterexample hunter reported BROKEN at HIGH confidence against the novelty claim, naming four prior-art counterexamples. Opened one by one: one accurate (The Conversation, 30 April 2026 -- the closing sentence is verbatim what the hunter quoted); one partly accurate (a Substack that states the mode-of-use thesis but cites only the favourable evidence); and two -- Stanford SCALE and Education Week -- about a different distinction entirely, human-led versus AI-led tutoring delivery, which is not the teaching-versus-answering cognitive claim. The hunter also misdated the accurate one by four months.
errors.was: the hunter says BROKEN at HIGH confidence, so the claim is broken
errors.should_have_been: The hunter produces candidate counterexamples, not verdicts. Each one is opened, read, and matched against the actual proposition before it is allowed to kill anything. A source that shares the vocabulary is not a source that makes the claim.
errors.why_it_survived: We built the adversarial role to stop us believing ourselves, and then believed it without applying to it the rule we already had for everything else: verifying that a source SAYS X is not verifying X. The role's own output is a source. Half of what it returned would not have survived the source ledger.

errors.caught_by: the operator saying he had received the email
errors.summary: I told the operator the corrected issue-two email was still unsent, because the board offered a 'Send the corrected email' action. The record shows it was sent at 14:33:42Z, which is 10:33 his time, matching the copy in his inbox. The button was offering a RE-send: the email file had changed by one word 23 minutes after the send, so its sha no longer matched the announce record. An action being available is not evidence the action has never been taken.
errors.was: the board offers Send, therefore nothing has been sent
errors.should_have_been: State of the world comes from published.json, not from what the dashboard is willing to let you do. Before reporting that something has or has not happened, read the record that would say so.
errors.why_it_survived: The sha-binding fix we built was correct and did exactly its job -- it reopened the action because the content changed. Nothing was wrong with the machine. What was wrong was reading an affordance as a history, and repeating it to the operator across three messages without once opening the file that records it.

errors.caught_by: the operator asking whether the email had been changed again
errors.summary: Every check this publication has runs inside publish.py. The deploy serves whatever lands on the default branch. So an ordinary `git commit` and `git push` puts a page in front of a reader with no preflight, no gate, no record -- and that is how a one-word fix to issue two went live at 14:56 while published.json still described the 14:26 version. Checking for it afterwards found the same thing had happened to issue one: a nav link added on 29 August, live, unrecorded. Two of two published issues were serving content nothing had signed off on.
errors.was: the gates are thorough, therefore what is published has been through them
errors.should_have_been: A gate that only fires on one path is not a gate, it is a convention. The check has to live where the content leaves -- at the push -- or it protects nothing.
errors.why_it_survived: Nobody looked. The record is in the repo precisely so it can be diffed against reality, and for two days nothing diffed it. The fix is a pre-push hook that compares the page's content hash on the branch being pushed against the last publication record, plus `publish.py record-live` so a change too small for the front door still gets written down instead of pushed past the guard with --no-verify.

errors.caught_by: issue two's preflight blocking on eleven counterexample verdicts about subjects it does not mention
errors.summary: counterexample.py resolves a slug through source_ledger.case_dir, which only knows issues/WHU-nnn-<slug>. Candidate-stage hunts are about leads, which live in issues/leads/<slug>. With no lead resolvable, seven hunts -- on minors' social-media access, on Australia's impact analysis, on AI and cognition -- were written into issues/WHU-002-cdk46/counterexample/ because cdk46 was the slug that resolved. They then read as unadjudicated adverse findings against issue two.
errors.was: the wrong directory is untidy
errors.should_have_been: A finding in the wrong case file is a false finding about that piece, indistinguishable from a real one, and it blocks the piece it was never about. Leads resolve first, and a bare-claim hunt into a published case file must be asked for twice.
errors.why_it_survived: The tool took a slug and never asked whether the slug named the thing being examined. It was easier to reuse a resolvable slug than to make the lead directory the tool would accept.

errors.caught_by: the operator forwarding a Reddit thread
errors.summary: Six rounds of targeted search plus a purpose-built lead scanner did not surface Shaw & Nave's 'Cognitive Surrender' — three PREREGISTERED experiments, N = 1,372, 9,593 trials, posted on SSRN in February 2026. On preregistration it is the most rigorous study in the whole set, and it identifies a mechanism neither of the two literatures we had assembled contains. A stranger on Reddit had it.
errors.was: we searched the literature
errors.should_have_been: We searched journals and the press. Working-paper repositories are a separate habitat with separate indexing — SSRN, NBER, OSF/PsyArXiv, and the economics and business-school preprint series — and a question that touches productivity, decision-making or behaviour will have work sitting in them that a journal search never returns. Each is its own search step, by name.
errors.why_it_survived: The scanner was built to find BELIEFS in coverage, which it does. Nothing in the process was built to find the best EVIDENCE, and we assumed that following the belief's citations would lead to it. It leads only to what the belief already cites.

errors.caught_by: the operator obtaining the PDF a machine could not fetch
errors.summary: For several hours the file recorded, from a single blog post, that the corrected effect size was read off Wang & Fan's FOREST plot and that the authors never responded to correspondence. The paper says FUNNEL plot, and says the authors replied promptly and blamed a typesetting error. One of those is a detail; the other would have printed an unfairness about two named academics.
errors.was: six outlets reported the retraction, so the specifics are well attested
errors.should_have_been: Six outlets reporting one audit is one source. Every specific about what a paper found is a claim about that paper, and it is checked in that paper. Where the paper cannot be opened by machine, it is opened by a person before anything from it is printed — which is the rule we wrote after issue two and had not yet had to use.
errors.why_it_survived: The ledger DID hold it correctly — S005 blocked, S015 marked as deriving from it, used_for set to 'NOTHING YET'. The machinery worked. What nearly failed was the prose around it: the specifics were repeated to the operator in conversation as though established, three times, while the file beside them said they were not.

errors.caught_by: running the entry gate on the candidate after four reframes
errors.summary: The entry gate returned ok on nine of ten rows for a candidate whose central fields still described the FIRST of four framings. 'What the sources show' described a mode-of-use split we had abandoned; the kill condition named a test we had already run and superseded; 'our contribution' named a claim the counterexample hunter had already broken.
errors.was: the gate checks the premise
errors.should_have_been: The gate checks that a field is FILLED, not that it is CURRENT. A premise that has been reframed is a premise whose answers are stale by default, and a gate that cannot tell the difference is measuring paperwork. At minimum it should compare the recorded kill-condition test against the recorded kill condition and warn when the condition has changed since the test.
errors.why_it_survived: Every check we have asks whether something was recorded. Almost none asks whether what was recorded is still true. The same shape as the announce-sha problem, in a different place: a verdict unbound from the thing it judged.

errors.caught_by: reading a scoping review against two papers we had already read at source
errors.summary: A peer-reviewed scoping review of AI deskilling — the document a doctor would read to find out what this literature says — calls a retrospective observational study 'a multicenter randomized trial' in its abstract, and attaches a description of a 2023 automation-bias experiment (27 radiologists, incorrect BI-RADS suggestions) to a citation for a different 2025 paper that found AI improved accuracy. We caught both only because we had read both underlying papers ourselves that evening.
errors.was: a systematic or scoping review is a safe place to take a study's description from
errors.should_have_been: A review is another hop, and caveats fall off at every hop. Any claim taken from a review about what a primary study found is checked in the primary study, exactly as a claim taken from a news article is. The safest-looking hop is the one where nobody checks.
errors.why_it_survived: We were about to use the review to answer a question that decided the piece's confidence — is this one study or a pattern — and we would have taken its characterisations with it. The only reason we did not is that we happened to have read two of its sources hours earlier.

errors.caught_by: the counterexample hunter, at HIGH confidence, correctly
errors.summary: We proposed that a narrowing of visual search measured in radiologists was a plausible mechanism for the detection loss measured in endoscopists, and asserted that no published work linked the two or tested the mechanism. It had been measured IN ENDOSCOPY in 2022 by Troya et al., who raised deskilling themselves; Troya sits in the reference list of the very paper we were linking from; and a Stanford commentary we had already opened that evening proposes exactly that mechanism and cites it.
errors.was: nobody has connected these
errors.should_have_been: Before asserting that a link between two findings is unmade, read the reference list of both papers. This is the CHAIN_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS error inverted — there we asserted a link without checking for a citation; here we asserted the absence of one without checking either. Both are claims about the relationship between documents made without opening them.
errors.why_it_survived: It felt like an insight, and insights are the thing this process is worst at doubting. The saving grace is that the hunt ran BEFORE drafting, so the sentence was struck before it was ever written.

errors.caught_by: the same hunt naming a page we had already opened
errors.summary: We fetched Zhou's ACG commentary on the colonoscopy study and asked it for the study's limitations. It gave them, and we moved on. It also contained the proposed mechanism and the citation that made our own hypothesis redundant. We found that out hours later from an adversarial role that searched the open web.
errors.was: we read that source
errors.should_have_been: A targeted fetch answers the question asked and hides everything else. A source the piece will rely on is read for what it CONTAINS, not for what we went to it for — and the ledger should record which question was asked, so 'machine_read' does not overstate what was seen.
errors.why_it_survived: The ledger records access state, not the question asked. Every 'sections' field on this issue is really a list of what we asked for.

errors.caught_by: the second counterexample hunt on the reframed claim
errors.summary: After two hunts narrowed our novelty claim, what remained was a four-part conjunction that survived only because no single piece had assembled all four elements — the colonoscopy loss, the mammography experiments, the null result and the limitations. Each element had been carried by somebody. The claim was technically true and rhetorically worthless.
errors.was: the claim survived the hunt, so we can make it
errors.should_have_been: When a novelty claim survives only by adding conjuncts, it has already failed. Retire it and find something DEMONSTRABLE instead. Here the replacement was better: rather than asserting that nobody has assembled this, show five named carriers that each dropped the caveats. A thing you can exhibit beats a thing you can only assert.
errors.why_it_survived: Surviving the adversary felt like passing, and each narrowing looked like a refinement rather than a retreat. Three narrowings in one day should have been the signal.

errors.caught_by: testing our own kill condition before drafting
errors.summary: We proposed that the caveats on the colonoscopy deskilling study fall off at every hop, listed five named carriers that dropped them, told the operator this was demonstrable rather than asserted, and treated it as the piece's thesis. One deliberate search for the disconfirming case found it in the first result: the Science Media Centre published expert reaction on the day of publication, with three named academics, one of whom named the exact confounder we believed nobody had carried.
errors.was: we can exhibit five instances, so the pattern is shown rather than claimed
errors.should_have_been: Five instances chosen by us, to demonstrate a pattern we proposed, is a selected sample until somebody searches for the counter-instances on purpose. Exhibiting examples is not evidence of a pattern; it is evidence that examples exist. The search that would disprove it has to be run, and run before the claim is made, not after.
errors.why_it_survived: Retiring the novelty claim in favour of 'something demonstrable' felt like a tightening of standards, and the new claim inherited none of the scepticism the old one had earned. A claim that replaces a broken one starts at zero, not at the credibility of the process that broke it.

errors.caught_by: re-reading the entry before committing it
errors.summary: Ten minutes after writing a module whose docstring says an unrun check must not look like a check that found nothing, the first check recorded against the first watch list we ever built listed four searches — including a Retraction Watch sweep of every source and a ClinicalTrials.gov search for a crossover trial — and two of them had not been run. The list had been written from the watch's QUESTIONS rather than from what actually happened.
errors.was: recording that the watch ran
errors.should_have_been: A check records what was DONE, never what was due. The temptation is structural: the questions are sitting right there in the file, they read like a checklist, and filling them in feels like completing the form rather than making a claim. It is a claim.
errors.why_it_survived: It did not — it was corrected the same evening, before it reached a page. But it survived long enough to be written, and it would have been the single most damaging thing in this issue: a living page whose freshness promise rests on a check that says it searched places it did not search.

errors.caught_by: lint_claims blocking a name with no record that anyone opened the author list
errors.summary: Hours after recording the standing rule that a systematic or scoping review is a hop and not a source, and that every description of a primary study taken from a review must be verified in that primary study, the draft carried a whole paragraph of figures lifted from that same review's summary table: 32 radiology residents, sensitivity up 12 points, reading time down 18%, performance stable at a three-month follow-up. The paper has EIGHT residents, reports mean absolute error and inter-rater agreement rather than sensitivity or reading time, and contains no three-month follow-up at all. It had been given prominence on the page as the null result the piece was honour-bound to carry.
errors.was: the review reports the study's figures, so we can report them
errors.should_have_been: The rule as written. What made it break was that the paragraph FELT like scrupulousness — it was the finding that cut against our own argument, and carrying it was the honest thing to do, which made its provenance invisible. A figure that flatters the other side gets the same sourcing as one that flatters ours.
errors.why_it_survived: It did not reach a page, and the reason is worth stating exactly: nothing about the figures caught it. What caught it was a check on the NAME. lint_claims blocks any 'X and colleagues' with no record that somebody opened the author list — a check built after issue two published 'Jacot and colleagues' for a paper by Tanguy. Opening the author list meant opening the paper, and the paper was not the study we had described. A check aimed at surnames caught a wrong study.

errors.caught_by: the counterexample verdict check, at the first full preflight
errors.summary: Three adjudications were written by replacing the first occurrence of the string 'VERDICT: ' in the file. The first occurrence is in the template's instruction block at the top — 'VERDICT: broken | narrowed | survived — yours, not the role's'. The real, empty VERDICT line at the foot of each section stayed empty. The verdicts read fine to a person scrolling the file and were invisible to the check that looks for them.
errors.was: the adjudication is written down
errors.should_have_been: Written where the check reads. A record that satisfies a human reading the file and not the machine that gates on it is worse than no record, because it looks done.
errors.why_it_survived: Nothing surfaced it until the full preflight ran for the first time, which needed the summary email to exist. Two of these had been reported to the operator as adjudicated, and in substance they were — the reasoning was real and is now in the right place.

errors.caught_by: looking again, in the place the thing actually lives
errors.summary: The operator said we had decided on a cap of two gate passes. I searched the known-errors fixture, the whatholdsup scripts and docs, found nothing, and told him I could not find a record of it and that the precedent ran the other way. RUNS_PER_CYCLE = 2 is defined in scripts/signal/factcheck_draft.py, one directory over, with a comment giving the exact reasoning he had described.
errors.was: I searched and it is not there
errors.should_have_been: I searched three places and it was not in them. The gate's cap lives in the gate, which is the first place to look and the one place I did not. An absence is only as wide as the search behind it, and a search that stops at the directory you expected is not a search of the repository.
errors.why_it_survived: It did not survive long, but it produced the worst kind of wrong: telling a person their own recollection of their own project was unsupported, on the strength of a partial grep. The same failure shape as asserting nobody had linked two findings without reading either reference list.

errors.caught_by: a preflight row saying 11 sentences differed from what readers see now, on a page we believed nobody could see
errors.summary: The issue-three draft was written to site/whatholdsup/deskilling.html, which is the deploy path. Every push put it on the public web. It was live at whatholdsup.org/deskilling for six commits — 47,214 bytes, HTTP 200 — ungated, un-reviewed, with no counterexample hunt completed and no outside review, under a masthead reading 'Published 30 August 2026'. Nothing linked to it and it was not in the sitemap, which is luck and not a control.
errors.was: the guard stops unreviewed content reaching readers
errors.should_have_been: The guard compares a PUBLISHED page against its publication record. A page that has never been published has no record to differ from, so it was invisible: the guard protected the two live issues and was blind to a third simply appearing. Presence at the deploy path is publication. A draft belongs in its issue directory until the publish step moves it.
errors.why_it_survived: Every preceding issue was drafted straight into site/ and published within a day, so the window never opened. Issue three spent a day and a half in draft with a page that said Published. And the check that finally caught it was not looking for this at all — 'correction recorded' compares the page against the live version, and it found a live version because there was one. Read as a bug for twenty minutes before it was read as a fact.

standing_rules: The draft's bibliography is never evidence. Every figure is re-derived from a source the checker locates itself.
Unverified is a failure, not a warning. A check that could not run is not a pass.
Any claim about what a third party did, said or omitted requires named, checked instances before it ships.
A claim that the coverage got something right is a publishable outcome. The delta section must not require a scalp.
CANNOT VERIFY is a statement about the checker's reach, never about whether the fact exists. It may not be written up as 'appears in no source'.

Internal claims — our rubric, our arithmetic, our corrections policy, our own editorial history — are recorded for a human to check, never counted as source failures. A gate that blocks on 'we acknowledge within 48 hours' is a gate people learn to override.

An unsupported claim about what other outlets did has now been introduced three separate times, twice while fixing something else. Any sentence asserting what coverage did, failed to do, or rarely does requires named instances or must be cut.
The gate's own findings are checked before they are acted on. Three of its flags were false positives traced to matching a figure against the wrong readout of the same trial.

The failure mode of a publication whose job is finding what coverage missed is to make the missing qualification sound more devastating than it is. Every individual sentence stays defensible while the impression does not. Test: would this sentence survive being read aloud by someone who believes the underlying result?

Confidence in DIRECTION and confidence in MAGNITUDE are separate questions and no single verdict, score or headline can express both. A positive topline from a large blinded trial warrants high confidence in the first and near-zero in the second, at the same time.

A NOT_FOUND is a statement about our reach, not about the world. Before acting on one, open the URL if one exists anywhere in the run. Where two roles disagree about the same source, the disagreement is the finding.

Before a draft goes to the gate, every figure on the page is diffed against the working brief it came from. The brief is not evidence - it is a record of what we decided we knew - but a figure on the page that is not in the brief, or a column in the brief that is not on the page, is a transcription question that must be answered before spending a gate run on it.

A guideline, a review or a press release may be cited for what it says and for pointing at a trial. It is never the source of a trial's figures. Every number in a table of ours is re-derived from the trial publication, and one trial's figures all come from the same analysis.

A before/after comparison of the gate against itself is not evidence at n = 1. The gate is a sampler: two runs of the same fixture disagree on about half their rows. Any claim that a change to the prompts or the recall brief helped or hurt requires at least three runs per arm, and the claim is about the rates, not about any single row.

When a limit is raised because something hit it, grep for every other use of that limit before moving on. A constant that was wrong once is wrong everywhere it appears, and the second failure will arrive later and look like a new problem.

No finding that asserts something about a third party's document may be written onto a page until somebody has opened that document and read the sentence. This binds findings the gate generates as hard as it binds claims we write ourselves -- harder, because a finding arrives looking like a check that has already happened.

Two gate runs per draft before outside review, one after. Enforced in code by RUNS_PER_CYCLE, overridable only with --past-cap and a written reason. Issue two was gated eighteen times for $66.76, of which about $27 bought nothing and one run put a false claim into the page.

A finding dismissed three times on the same reasoning gets read again, properly, by someone who has not written the earlier dismissals -- or its dismissal is escalated to the operator. A repeat finding is evidence the role is confident, not evidence it is broken. Recorded after 1.015 was dismissed seven times and upheld on the eighth.
A claim verified only as a quotation may be published only as a quotation, with attribution. Verifying that a source says X is not verifying X, and the scope of the source's sentence travels with it.

Every universal negative on the page -- no trial has, nobody has, none exists -- gets one adversarial search whose only job is to find a counterexample, and that search must include the trial registries and the regulatory reviews, not only the literature.

Before writing that something could not be established, search ClinicalTrials.gov's results tab, the FDA review documents and the EMA assessment report. Two of five findings in the second post-publication review were facts declared unknowable that sit in a registry.

Any proper noun introduced onto the page from gate output -- an author, an institution, a trial name -- is verified against the source before it ships. 'Jacot and colleagues' was printed from a COVERAGE finding while fixing an attribution gap; the paper is by Tanguy et al.

Before a candidate is drafted, run the counterexample hunter on the novelty claim itself -- 'nobody has already made this argument' -- with the same instruction to find one instance. Two consecutive issues had their central contribution already in print, one found by a reviewer after publication and one by the kill condition before drafting.

The novelty test is not 'has anyone published this' but 'has anyone published this where a general reader would find it'. A finding established in a journal and absent from the coverage is a subject; a finding absent from both is usually a sign we have not looked hard enough.

A claim that one document is carrying, repeating or responding to another is a claim about a citation. Open the citing document and find the reference before writing it. A headline that sounds like a study's conclusion is not evidence that it came from that study.

The counterexample hunter returns candidates, not verdicts. Every counterexample it names is opened and read before it is allowed to narrow or kill a claim, and it is matched against the proposition rather than the vocabulary. Its confidence rating is not evidence. Half of one high-confidence break was off-target on inspection.

When a hunt for prior art returns a near miss, ask what the near miss did NOT do. A piece that states our sentence but does not show the evidence behind it has taken the headline, not the subject. That is a narrowing of the novelty claim, not the end of it -- and the narrowed claim must then be stated in the piece, crediting whoever got there first.

Never report to the operator that something was or was not published, sent or accepted from the state of a button. Open published.json and read the record. The board reflects what may be done next, not what has been done.

Every check must fire on the path the content actually takes to a reader, not only on the path we intend to use. Ask of each gate: what is the command that reaches the world without passing through this?

A finding is filed against a piece. Before writing one, confirm the slug names the piece the finding is about -- an adverse finding in the wrong case file is a false accusation the machine will enforce.

Search the working-paper repositories by name as their own step — SSRN, NBER, OSF/PsyArXiv, arXiv — before concluding what the evidence on a question is. Following a belief's citations finds only what the belief already cites. The single most rigorous study behind issue three was on SSRN and no journal or press search returned it.

A fairness claim about a named person — that they did not answer, did not correct, did not respond — is held to the strictest sourcing on the page. It is checked in the primary document, never taken from coverage, and the other half of the story is looked for on purpose. Wang and Fan answered their critics within days; only the retraction correspondence went unanswered, and reporting the second without the first would have been false.

A recorded answer is bound to the question it answered. When a premise is reframed, every field written for the old framing is stale until rewritten, and a gate that reports 'ok' on a filled field is reporting paperwork. Bind the kill-condition test to the kill-condition text, as acceptances are bound to a sha.

Read the adversary's DISCARD PILE, not only its verdict. The counterexample hunter lists what it reviewed and set aside; on issue three the two best sources in the file — a Nature Medicine Perspective that gave the piece its frame, and a FAccT paper — were sitting in that list, classified as 'not general-audience' and therefore not reported as counterexamples. The role is a search we paid for; taking only its conclusion throws most of it away.

A systematic or scoping review is a hop, not a source. Every description of a primary study taken from a review is verified in that primary study before it is printed. On issue three a peer-reviewed review promoted an observational study to a randomised trial in its own abstract and mis-cited an automation-bias experiment to a paper that found the opposite.
Before asserting that nobody has linked two findings, read the reference lists of both papers. The link is most often already inside the one you are arguing from.

Record in the ledger WHAT QUESTION was asked of each source, not only that it was opened. A targeted fetch answers what it was asked and conceals the rest; on issue three a commentary read for its limitations also held the mechanism that made one of our claims redundant.

A novelty claim that survives only by accumulating conjuncts has failed. Retire it and replace it with something demonstrable — named instances a reader can check — rather than an absence a reader must take on trust.

When the piece demonstrates a pattern from named instances, look on purpose for the instances that would contradict it and count honestly. Five examples chosen by us, to show a pattern we proposed, is the shape of a selected sample whether or not it is one.
