Before asserting a pattern from named instances, run the search designed to find the counter-instances, and record what it returns even when it returns nothing. On issue three the first such search overturned the thesis in its first result.
A claim that replaces a broken claim starts at zero. It inherits none of the credibility of the process that broke its predecessor, and it gets the same adversarial treatment the first one got.

A recorded check lists what was searched, not what the watch asks. Any question not actually checked is written into the record as not checked. The form is not the work, and filling in the form is a claim about the work.

A living issue needs three ways to change a published page, not one. `publish` for a rewrite, `update` for the ordinary event of a new study changing two paragraphs, `record-live` for a change too small to touch the argument. With only the first, nobody keeps updating, and a page displaying a changelog that is never updated is worse than a page that never promised.

Exemption lists fail closed. UPDATE_SOFTENS names the checks an update does not re-earn; anything absent from it blocks, including checks added later. A list of exemptions will be forgotten, so it has to be forgotten safely.

A figure that cuts against our own argument is sourced exactly as strictly as one that supports it. Carrying the other side's best evidence feels like scrupulousness, and that feeling is what hides where the figure came from.

Checks catch things they were not aimed at, which is an argument for keeping the cheap deterministic ones even when they seem pedantic. The attribution check exists to stop a wrong surname; on issue three it stopped a wrong study.

Write a record where the check reads it, not merely into the file. A first-occurrence string replacement lands in the template's instructions; verify by re-running the check that gates on it, never by re-reading the file.

Before telling anyone a record does not exist, search the component that would own it, not only the places you have been working. State the scope of the search alongside the conclusion: 'not in X, Y or Z' is a finding; 'it is not there' is a claim about the whole repository.

The gate's cycle is two runs, reset by the outside review, with one run after the review to close it. The reason is on the record: all three of issue two's outside-review findings survived fourteen gate runs, and the single worst error in that piece was GENERATED by the gate and could not have been caught by running it again. Going past the cap requires --past-cap and a reason.

The gate is scoped to FACTS and INFERENCES. A finding about word choice, emphasis, tone or framing is adjudicated once and closed; it is not iterated on. Accuracy and fairness are the touchstone, and there is no version of a sentence that every reader reads identically — treating that as a defect to be fixed produces an endless loop and buys nothing.

Presence at the deploy path IS publication. A draft lives in its issue directory and the publish step moves it; nothing under site/ is ever a work in progress. The pre-push guard now refuses any top-level page there that is neither a standing site page nor an issue with a publication record.
A masthead that says Published is a claim, and it is false on an ungated draft. If a draft must carry a date line at all, it says what it is.

second_pass.result: BLOCKED. Found the two DROPPED errors above and the OVERSTATED one, plus two minor fairness points (a rounded interval in the summary strip inconsistent with the body, and an unsupported claim about which figure 'travelled' in coverage). It also produced 13 NOT_FOUND verdicts of which 8 were internal claims it had no way to check — the flaw that prompted the scope field.

third_pass.regression_on_corrected_piece: BLOCKED, 5 external claims unverified of 36 (was 13 of 42 before the scope fix). Four genuine findings: an unsupported claim that 'nobody else has' noted the investigator-assessed endpoint; 'the one least often quoted' as an unsupported claim about coverage; 30-month absolute rates quoted in a section discussing five-year results when five-year rates (68.8% vs 49.1%) exist; and a framing that made a nominal p-value in a descriptive analysis sound improper. All four fixed.
third_pass.false_positives: Three. The adverse-event rates (fatigue 59.6%, injection-site pain 59.6%, chills 51.0%) were flagged WRONG_VALUE against a 2023 release; they are verbatim in the five-year release and are correct. 'n=14' was flagged as misrepresenting an event count; the release says '(n=14)' and it is 14 deaths. The ASCO Post date was flagged unconfirmed in one run and confirmed exactly in the other.
third_pass.nondeterminism: The two runs disagreed with each other on the ASCO Post date and on the adverse-event rates, from near-identical inputs. The gate's own findings need verifying before they are acted on, exactly as a draft's do.
third_pass.fixture_result: Six of eight planted errors caught cleanly, including the invented p = 0.0031 identified as appearing in no source for any timepoint, and the contradiction between a Checking note calling figures unverifiable and the body printing them. Two partial: the stale irAE rates were not isolated, and the missing grade 3+ toxicity was not flagged as an omission. One fixture construction flaw: the Checking footer still carried corrected-version text, so the DMFS easing phrase leaked into a draft that was supposed to omit it.

how_to_add_one: When something wrong reaches a reader — a correction email, a mistake noticed after publishing, a figure that turns out not to hold — add an entry with caught_by 'nothing' and say in why_it_survived which role should have caught it and why it did not. Then add an instance of that class to factcheck_broken_fixture.html and its answer key, so the recall test measures it from then on. An entry that is never seeded is a note, not a test.

kinds.draft: An error in the writing. Goes to the role that should catch it, as a checklist of what to look for.
kinds.instrument: A defect in the gate itself — a role that returned the wrong answer, or the wrong shape of answer. Goes to the role that made it, as a description of its own failure mode. owned_by names that role, since caught_by will say a human.
kinds.process: Neither. A failure of what was checked, or when. No role can find these in a draft and none is given them; they are fixed in code.
